umbrella_banners.note: IFRS statements print EQUITY AND LIABILITIES above the Equity, Non-current and Current sub-banners; reading it as equity would refuse every liability line item beneath it.
Schedule III prints ASSETS as an umbrella over the Non-Current and Current sub-banners. Reading it as a section of its own would scope every asset line to a section no concept declares.

exclusive_vocabularies.note: IAS 7 divides cash flows into exactly three activities and a statement labels each subtotal with its own, so naming one rules out the others.

normalisation.note: Applied to every candidate row label and every alias before comparison. The quoted literals in each step are that step's own vocabulary — `row_reconstruct._quoted_examples` harvests them — so they are configuration, not illustration.
pipeline: Full-width to half-width punctuation; map ╱ ／ ⁄ to /; map （） to ().

Strip footnote and note markers: trailing digits in parentheses, superscripts, '(note 12)', '(Refer note 36)', '(Refer Note 2A)', and the asterisk, caret, hash and dagger an Indian filing hangs off a caption to key it to a sub-note: '*', '^', '#', '†'.
Strip leading numbering and bullets: '1.', '(a)', '(i)', 'A.', '-'. Schedule III numbers its own sub-captions this way.
Strip trailing colons and dashes used to introduce sub-captions ('Trade Payables:', 'Total Outstanding dues of -').

Strip inline unit and currency annotations: '(₹ in Crores)', '(₹ in Lakhs)', '(` in Crores)', '(` in crores)', 'Rs. in crores', 'Rs. in lakhs', 'INR in million', '₹', '(unaudited)', '(Audited)'. THE GRAVE ACCENT IS NOT A TYPO: an Indian PDF whose font lacks the ₹ glyph substitutes ` for it, and both forms occur in one document.
Collapse internal whitespace to a single space; strip zero-width characters and soft hyphens.
Join a wrapped caption to its continuation line before matching, then also retain the bare fragment as a fallback candidate.
normalisation.wrapped_caption_rule:
A Schedule III statement prints a mandatory 'Note No.' column BETWEEN the caption and the figures, and its captions are long enough to wrap in the width that leaves: 'Total Outstanding dues of creditors other than Micro Enterprises' / 'and Small Enterprises' is one caption on two physical lines, and read as two it matches neither. Reassemble from the value row upward before matching; match the reassembled string first, and use the bare fragment only if that fails.

THE NOTE COLUMN IS NOT A FIGURE. That same mandatory column is numeric and sits left of the amounts, so its value is the first number on the row and reads as the current period unless it is removed. Resolve it geometrically where the column can be located and by shape otherwise — a bare one- or two-digit integer, optionally suffixed A or B ('2A', '4B', '11A'), followed on the row by a real amount.

binding.note: Precedence is section-first. A concept can only claim a row printed inside one of its section_scope values.
order: 1. Resolve the statement (balance_sheet / profit_and_loss / cash_flow) from the page or table caption.

2. Resolve the printed section from the nearest preceding section header. If no header is resolvable, the row is unbound: route to review, never guess a section. (A row WITH a resolved section that no concept claims is not unbound — it is swept into that section's residual; see unbound_row_policy.)
3. Restrict the candidate concept set to concepts whose section_scope contains the resolved section.
4. Rule tier: exact normalised alias, then regex_hints, in descending match_priority. Any exclude_hints hit is a hard veto, not a score penalty.
5. Semantic tier over the restricted set only, using definition + include + exclude. Never over the full ontology.
6. Tie between concepts listed in each other's confusable_with: resolve with section_disambiguation; if still tied, emit both as candidates and route to review. Never pick by declaration order.
7. Residual sweep (see residual_framework) runs last, over rows no dedicated concept claimed.
8. Reconcile the section against its reported subtotal.
binding.unbound_row_policy: Route an unclaimed face value only to the residual for its resolved printed section. Never borrow a neighbouring concept or cross a section. After all mapping and gap-closing opportunities, the engine-level face_mapping_contract gives any remaining face value a unique engine_unclassified_face key outside the ontology/template namespaces. This keeps the row stored and reviewable without feeding it into an unrelated calculation. Verified non-additive aggregates replaced by mapped components remain evidence-only.
binding.match_priority: Integer 0-99, higher evaluated first. Long specific captions rank above short generic ones so 'Total assets less current liabilities' cannot be pre-empted by 'Total current liabilities' on token overlap. Residuals are 0 and unreachable by matching.

prompt: ICON is an Indian bank credit-monitoring (CMA-style) spread: an operating statement, an analysis of the balance sheet, and contingent liabilities with other information, filled from a borrower's financial statements. Filings may follow Ind AS (Schedule III, Division II) or Indian GAAP (Revised Schedule VI), and are often scaled in lakhs or crores; do not assume either from the units alone. Extract only figures supported by filing citations. Keep standalone and consolidated reporting separate. Preserve reporting date, period duration, presentation currency and scale. Distinguish raw-material consumption from closing inventory, period charges from accumulated balances, funded borrowing from guarantees, and recognised liabilities from unprovided exposure. Do not treat unavailable as zero or calculate amounts in a citation-only answer.

sign_convention.stored_value: The reported value after paren-to-negative conversion.
sign_convention.expenses_and_outflows: Stored POSITIVE, as printed. The ICON template subtracts expense lines the way the CMA workbook does (Net Sales = Total less Excise duty; Operating Profit = Total operating income less operating expenses), so an expense is never negated on load.
sign_convention.unsigned_source: A filing that prints expenses as unsigned positives is read as printed; nothing is negated.
sign_convention.either: Subtotals, working-capital movements, fair-value changes, share of results, OCI and net cash flows are sign-indeterminate. Retain the reported sign; never coerce.
sign_convention.validation: A concept whose sign_convention is positive_expected or negative_expected but whose loaded value carries the opposite sign is a review trigger, not an auto-correction.

global_rules.face_only_default: Concepts default to face_only: true. Notes are evidence for a face amount, never an independent source of one, unless note_use is decomposition_allowed.
global_rules.duplicate_fact_rule: The same economic fact on the face and in a note is one fact with multiple evidence references, not two additive values. This also applies to two face captions that report the same amount (see equivalence blocks).
parent_child_allocation: Never load a gross parent and its separately mapped children additively.
Residual = reported parent minus confirmed included children.
Subtract only on explicit inclusion wording, hierarchy, reconciliation or arithmetic support.
If containment is uncertain, retain the parent as evidence and route to review.
global_rules.no_fabricated_split: Never invent a decomposition. Where only a combined figure is reported, load the combined concept and leave the children empty. The one exception is a concept declaring sole_component_of: assigning a whole undifferentiated figure to a single child divides nothing, and it is refused as soon as any sibling child is evidenced on the face or in the subtotal's own note.
global_rules.totals_policy: Compute totals from mutually exclusive concept outputs. Use reported totals only for validation, never as an input to the components.

scope_selection.note: An Indian annual report presents the STANDALONE and the CONSOLIDATED financial statements in full, one after the other, in the same document — so the entity has to be resolved for two complete sets of statements, not for two columns of one.

entity_scope.rule: Resolve the entity from the statement's own title and column headings, never from position. An Indian filing titles them 'Balance Sheet' / 'Consolidated Balance Sheet' and 'Statement of Profit and Loss' / 'Consolidated Statement of Profit and Loss'; the standalone set is usually printed first and the consolidated set after it, but neither order is universal. Record entity_scope on every fact and never mix the two sets within one statement.
company_only_markers: Presence of Investments in subsidiaries on the face is strong evidence the statement is STANDALONE, since consolidation eliminates it. An Indian standalone balance sheet prints 'Investments in Subsidiaries and Associates' as its own non-current caption, which the consolidated one replaces with 'Investments in Associates and Joint Ventures' accounted for under the equity method.

period_selection.rule: The Indian financial year ends 31 March, and columns are headed 'As at 31.03.2026' / 'As at 31st March 2026' on the balance sheet and 'Year 2025-26' or 'For the year ended 31st March 2026' on the profit and loss. Identify the current period from the heading date rather than from column position, and load comparatives only into the comparative slot.
period_selection.restatement_rule: Where a comparative is labelled restated, or reopened by a scheme of amalgamation or arrangement ('Restated balance as at 1st April 2024', 'Changes on account of amalgamation'), load it as the comparative and set restated: true. Keep both figures with the flag rather than overwriting an original comparative already loaded — a court- or NCLT-approved scheme routinely restates the opening balance sheet.

units_and_currency.rule: Resolve currency and scale from the statement header, not the cover page, and re-resolve per statement — an Indian report commonly states the financial statements in crores and a subsidiary schedule or a BRSR table in lakhs or absolute rupees. Persist unit on every fact; never normalise scale silently. 1 crore = 10 million = 100 lakh.
units_and_currency.conflict: If the header scale and a printed subtotal are inconsistent by a factor of 100 or 1,000, trust neither and route the statement to review. The factor of 100 is the one to watch on an Indian filing, because it is the lakh-to-crore step and a mis-read there is not an order of magnitude but two.

scope_selection.column_guard: Every fact carries the resolved (entity_scope, period, currency, unit). Two facts for the same canonical_key that differ on any of these are distinct facts, not duplicates — which is what keeps the standalone and the consolidated set of the same filing from colliding.

residual_framework.note: One definition governing the 11 output-template subsection residuals. Each uses an existing template line; no template row is added.

sweep.runs: after all dedicated concepts in the section have been resolved, before section reconciliation
sweep.candidate_set: every printed value row on the FACE of the statement whose resolved section equals the residual's single section_scope value
eligibility: The row printed a value for the selected entity_scope, period, currency and unit.
No dedicated concept whose section_scope contains this section claimed the row.

The row is not a section subtotal, statement total, section header, attribution caption, per-share figure, narrative row, note-reference-only row, truncated caption, an "of which" breakdown of the row above it or a sub-enumerated component of it ((a)… or 1.… beneath a numbered head) — each of those amounts is already inside the row above, so sweeping it counts the same money twice.
The row was printed INSIDE this section. A row printed in any other section is ineligible however similar its wording — there is no cross-section rescue.

The row's sign agrees with the section's sign_convention, where the section states one. A row signed against its section is evidence the SECTION is wrong, not the amount, so it goes to review rather than into the bucket — a cost swept into income moves the income subtotal and every total below it.
sweep.plug_behaviour: forbidden — the residual is never computed as (reported subtotal − mapped children)
sweep.literal_others_caption: A row captioned 'Others' or 'Miscellaneous' is simply one unmapped face row and sweeps in as a single component. It gets no privileged treatment and no dedicated concept.

itemisation.rule: The residual's value is the arithmetic sum of its components. Original labels and signs are always retained; a swept row is never relabelled to 'Others'.

reconciliation.identity: reported_section_subtotal − Σ(dedicated concepts in section) − Σ(residual components) = 0
reconciliation.tolerance: one rounding unit per contributing row
reconciliation.on_failure: Emit an unallocated_gap fact carrying the difference and route the section to review. Never adjust the residual, and never adjust a dedicated concept, to close the gap.
reconciliation.sections_without_reported_subtotal: If the section prints no subtotal, the residual is still itemised but is flagged unreconciled and carries lower confidence.

review_triggers: any single component exceeds 2% of |reported section subtotal|
a component label scored at or above the semantic threshold against a dedicated concept but was vetoed by exclude_hints
residual sign is opposite to the section's sign_convention
the section reconciliation emitted an unallocated_gap
prohibitions: Never populated by alias, regex or embedding match.
Never carries a value with no itemised components.
Never absorbs a row a dedicated concept could have claimed but was not tested for — all dedicated concepts in the section must be evaluated first.
Never spans sections, statements, periods, entity scopes or units.

items.label: Domestic Sales
items.definition: Sales of products and services to customers in India for the year, before excise duty. Ind AS filings print one face row, 'Revenue from operations'; the domestic/export split is in its note ('Sale of products - Domestic', 'Sale of services') or in the disaggregation of revenue / geographical segment note ('Within India'). Indian GAAP prints it in the 'Revenue from operations' note. Where only total sale of products is given with no geographical split, the whole is domestic. Other operating revenue (scrap, export incentives, job work) belongs to pl_icon__other_recurring_operating_income.
exclude_criteria: Other operating revenue such as scrap sales and export incentives

items.label: Export Sales
items.definition: Sales of products and services to customers outside India for the year, including deemed exports, before excise duty. Printed in the 'Revenue from operations' note ('Sale of products - Export', 'Export sales') or the geographical disaggregation ('Outside India'). Export incentives, duty drawback and RoDTEP/MEIS benefits are not sales: they are pl_icon__other_recurring_operating_income.
exclude_criteria: Export incentives, duty drawback, RoDTEP and MEIS benefits

items.label: Total
items.definition: Total: the sum of Domestic Sales and Export Sales, as the template computes it. Use complete inputs on the same entity basis, reporting date/period, currency and scale. Do not sum both a component and its descendants or treat missing inputs as reported zeros.

items.label: Less Excise Duty
items.definition: Excise duty included in gross sales and deducted to reach net sales: the 'Less: Excise duty' row of an Indian GAAP P&L or revenue note, or the 'Excise duty' expense row of an Ind AS P&L for periods before GST (July 2017). Positive magnitude. GST is never included in revenue and is not this line.
aliases: Excise duty on sale of goods
Excise duty on sale of products

en: Excise duty on sale of goods
Excise duty on sale of products

items.label: Net Sales (1 - 2)
items.definition: Net Sales (1 - 2): Total less Less Excise Duty, as the template computes it. Use complete inputs on the same entity basis, reporting date/period, currency and scale. Do not sum both a component and its descendants or treat missing inputs as reported zeros.

items.label: Other recurring income incidental to main business
items.definition: Operating income incidental to the main business: the 'Other operating revenue(s)' rows of the 'Revenue from operations' note - sale of scrap, export incentives, duty drawback, RoDTEP/MEIS, processing and job-work income, hire of equipment. 'Sale of services' printed beside 'Sale of products' is the business's own revenue and belongs to domestic or export sales, not here. Not 'Other income' (interest, dividends, disposal gains, fair-value gains), which is non-operating.
exclude_criteria: Interest, dividend and fair-value income in 'Other income'
aliases: Other recurring income incidental to main business

en: Other recurring income incidental to main business

items.label: Total operating income
items.definition: Total operating income: the sum of Net Sales (1 - 2) and Other recurring income incidental to main business, as the template computes it. Use complete inputs on the same entity basis, reporting date/period, currency and scale. Do not sum both a component and its descendants or treat missing inputs as reported zeros.

items.label: Raw materials
items.definition: Raw-material consumption expense, comprising imported and indigenous consumption. Not purchases unless adjusted for inventory movements, and not closing raw-material inventory.

items.definition: Imported raw materials and components consumed in the year: the 'Imported' row of the 'Value of imported and indigenous raw materials consumed' table (with its percentage), printed in or after the 'Cost of materials consumed' note. Not CIF value of imports, which measures purchases. Leave empty if the filing gives no imported/indigenous split.

items.label: Power and Fuel

items.label: Direct Labour (Factory wages & salaries)
items.definition: Factory labour: 'Contract labour charges', 'Labour charges', 'Wages' printed in the 'Other expenses' or 'Manufacturing expenses' note, or a factory wages row shown separately in 'Employee benefits expense'. When employee benefits expense is printed only as one total, it all belongs to pl_icon__salary_and_staff_expenses and this line is empty.

items.label: Other manufacturing expenses
items.definition: Other manufacturing expenses: the sum of Processing / Job Work Charges, Freight and Transportation Charges and Others, as the template computes it. Use complete inputs on the same entity basis, reporting date/period, currency and scale. Do not sum both a component and its descendants or treat missing inputs as reported zeros.

items.label: Processing / Job Work Charges
items.definition: Processing and job-work charges paid to outside parties for manufacture: 'Job work charges', 'Processing charges', 'Sub-contracting charges' in the 'Other expenses' or 'Manufacturing expenses' note. Construction or sub-contract costs of an EPC company printed as their own expense note are also cited here.

items.label: Freight and Transportation Charges
items.definition: Freight inward and transport of materials to the factory: 'Freight inward', 'Carriage inwards', 'Transportation charges' in the 'Other expenses' note. Freight outward / forwarding on sales is selling expense and belongs to pl_icon__sga_others.

items.label: Others
items.definition: The remaining manufacturing rows of the 'Other expenses' or 'Manufacturing expenses' note: repairs to plant and machinery, factory rent, insurance of plant, testing and inspection, other manufacturing expenses. Only rows that are clearly factory costs and that no other cost-of-sales line claims.
